courses.title: CompTIA A+: PC Hardware
courses.description: Core 1 hardware: the CPU, motherboard, memory, storage, power, and the connectors that tie a PC together.

content.intro: The CPU executes instructions; the motherboard connects everything. A+ expects you to identify sockets, chipsets, and form factors.

ul.t: parallel work; more cores help multitasking.
Intel LGA vs AMD AM4/AM5 — CPU must match the socket.
controls I/O between CPU, RAM, and buses.
PCIe slots (x16 for GPUs, x1 for cards).

note.text: Match CPU socket, RAM type, and form factor to the case/PSU before buying.

p: CPUs need cooling — heatsink + fan (air) or liquid. Apply thermal paste between CPU and heatsink; overheating causes throttling and shutdowns.

content.practice: List the three things that must be compatible between a CPU and a motherboard.

quiz.p: A CPU must match the motherboard's…
quiz.ex: The socket (LGA/AM4/AM5) must match the CPU.

quiz.p: Which form factor is the largest with the most expansion?
quiz.ex: ATX is the largest common form factor.

quiz.p: A GPU typically uses which slot?
quiz.ex: Graphics cards use the PCIe x16 slot.

content.intro: RAM holds data the CPU is actively using; storage keeps it long-term. Know the types and their speeds.

ul.t: SSD over PCIe — fastest common storage.

note.text: RAM is volatile (lost on power off); storage is non-volatile.

p: SATA connects HDDs/SSDs (data + power cables). M.2 slots take NVMe or SATA modules directly on the board.

content.practice: Rank HDD, SATA SSD, and NVMe SSD from slowest to fastest.

quiz.p: Which is volatile (cleared on power off)?
The fastest common storage interface is…

content.intro: The PSU powers everything; ports and connectors link peripherals. A+ tests connector identification.

ul.t: must exceed total system draw (GPU-heavy builds need more).
24-pin board, CPU 8-pin, PCIe for GPU, SATA for drives.

note.text: Never open a PSU — capacitors can hold a dangerous charge even unplugged.

ul.t: USB-A, USB-C; USB 3.x is faster (often blue).

p: Know input (keyboard, mouse, scanner) vs output (monitor, printer) and how they connect (USB, Bluetooth, wireless dongles).

content.practice: Name the PSU connector used for the motherboard, the CPU, and a GPU.

quiz.p: The main motherboard power connector is…
quiz.ex: The 24-pin ATX connector powers the board.

quiz.p: You should never open a PSU because…
quiz.ex: Stored charge in capacitors is a shock hazard.

content.intro: Monitors and graphics: display technologies, resolutions, and the video connectors A+ tests.

ul.t: most common; IPS = better color/angles, TN = faster/cheaper.

note.text: HDMI and DisplayPort carry audio+video; VGA/DVI are legacy (DVI can be digital).

content.practice: Match IPS, TN, and OLED to: best color, fastest response, deepest blacks.

quiz.p: Which panel type has the best color/viewing angles?
quiz.ex: IPS offers superior color and angles.

quiz.p: Which connector is digital and carries audio?

content.intro: Printer types and the laser imaging process — a classic A+ topic tested in detail.

ul: Processing → Charging → Exposing → Developing → Transferring → Fusing → Cleaning

note.text: Memorize the order; questions ask 'what happens after exposing?' (developing).

p: Laser: replace toner, use a maintenance kit. Inkjet: clean/align heads. Keep firmware updated.

content.practice: List the seven steps of the laser printing process in order.

quiz.p: Which printer uses toner and a fusing step?
quiz.ex: Laser printers fuse toner to paper.

quiz.p: The step right after Exposing is…

content.intro: Purpose-built PCs and redundant storage arrays.

note.text: RAID is not a backup — it protects against disk failure, not deletion/ransomware.

p: RAID 1 for simple redundancy; RAID 5 balances capacity and protection; RAID 10 for performance + redundancy.

content.practice: Which RAID gives redundancy with only two disks, and which needs at least three?

quiz.ex: Striping boosts speed but has no redundancy.

quiz.p: RAID is not a substitute for…

courses.title: CompTIA A+: Networking Basics
courses.description: Core 1 networking at A+ depth: addressing, ports and protocols, cabling, and small-office/home wireless.

content.intro: How devices find and talk to each other: IP addresses, ports, and the common protocols A+ expects you to recall.

ul.t: DHCP assigns IPs; DNS resolves names to IPs.

note.text: A+ expects these port numbers from memory.

p: TCP is reliable/ordered (web, email); UDP is fast/connectionless (streaming, DNS queries).

content.practice: Write the port numbers for HTTPS, DNS, SSH, and RDP.

content.intro: Copper and fiber carry the network. Know the categories, connectors, and when to use each.

p: Coaxial (RG-6) for cable internet/TV. Know max copper run ~100 m before signal loss.

content.practice: Which cable category would you choose for a 10 Gbps run, and what connector does it use?

quiz.p: Max recommended copper Ethernet run is about…

content.intro: Setting up and securing a small-office/home network — the everyday tech task A+ centers on.

ul.t: use WPA3 or WPA2-AES; never WEP.

note.text: WEP is broken — never use it.

p: A combo router does routing, switching, Wi-Fi, DHCP, and NAT. Port forwarding exposes an internal service; enable a firewall.

content.practice: List three steps to secure a new home router.

quiz.p: The strongest listed Wi-Fi security is…
Which band offers more range (less speed)?
First thing to change on a new router…

content.intro: The boxes that build a network — know what each does.

ul: PoE delivers power over Ethernet (APs, cameras)
A combo SOHO router bundles router+switch+AP+firewall

note.text: Out of ports? Add a switch. Need Wi-Fi? Add an AP. Segment/secure? Firewall/VLAN.

content.practice: Name the device that routes between networks vs the one that connects devices on the same LAN.

quiz.p: Which device connects LAN devices by MAC address?
quiz.ex: A switch forwards by MAC on the LAN.

quiz.p: Power over Ethernet (PoE) is useful for…
quiz.ex: PoE powers APs/cameras over the data cable.

content.intro: The services that make IP networks usable.

ul.t: many private IPs share one public IP.
logical network separation on a switch.

note.text: APIPA (169.254.x) = no DHCP. Loopback = 127.0.0.1.

content.practice: Explain what NAT does and why home networks rely on it.

o: Many private IPs share one public IP
quiz.ex: NAT maps private IPs to a public one.

content.intro: How sites and homes connect to the internet.

note.text: Fiber where available; satellite/cellular for remote sites where wired isn't feasible.

content.practice: Which connection type has the highest latency, and which is fastest/symmetrical?

quiz.p: The fastest, typically symmetrical option is…

courses.title: CompTIA A+: Mobile, Virtualization & Cloud
courses.description: Mobile device support plus the virtualization and cloud concepts now core to Core 1.

content.intro: Laptops and phones have their own components, connectors, and sync/security needs.

ul: Sync to cloud (contacts, photos) across devices

note.text: Screen lock, biometrics, remote wipe, and encryption protect lost devices.

content.practice: Name two components that differ physically between a laptop and a desktop.

quiz.p: Sharing a phone's cellular data to a laptop is…
Best protection for a lost phone's data…
quiz.ex: Remote wipe and encryption protect data.

content.intro: One physical machine runs multiple virtual machines via a hypervisor — foundational to modern IT.

ul.t: runs on an OS (VirtualBox, VMware Workstation) — desktops.

note.text: Need CPU virtualization (Intel VT-x/AMD-V) enabled in BIOS, plus enough RAM/CPU for each VM.

content.practice: Give an example of a Type 1 and a Type 2 hypervisor.

quiz.p: VirtualBox on your Windows laptop is…
Which BIOS feature must be enabled for VMs?

content.intro: Cloud delivers computing over the internet. A+ expects the service and deployment models.

note.text: On-demand, elastic (scale up/down), measured/pay-as-you-go, accessible anywhere.

content.practice: Classify Microsoft 365, an Azure VM, and a managed app platform as SaaS/IaaS/PaaS.

quiz.p: Renting a bare VM in the cloud is…

content.intro: Connecting mobile devices and configuring email — frequent help-desk tasks.

note.text: Use IMAP/Exchange for multi-device sync; secure ports (993/995) use TLS.

p: Verify server names/ports, credentials, and TLS. For corporate mail, the device may need to accept an MDM/security policy.

content.practice: A user wants email on phone and laptop kept in sync — IMAP or POP3, and which secure port?

quiz.p: Which protocol keeps mail synced across devices?

quiz.ex: Bluetooth devices pair (often with a PIN).

content.intro: Keeping mobile data synced and secure across the fleet.

ul: Sync to desktop or over Wi-Fi

note.text: BYOD often uses containerization to separate work and personal data.

content.practice: List three controls that protect a lost corporate phone.

quiz.p: Which centrally enforces mobile security policy?
Best protection for a lost phone's data…

content.intro: Laptop-specific components and field-replaceable parts.

note.text: Power off and remove the battery (if removable) before internal work; use ESD protection.

content.practice: Name three field-replaceable laptop parts.

quiz.p: Before internal laptop work you should…
quiz.ex: Power down and use ESD protection.

courses.title: CompTIA A+: Operating Systems
courses.description: Core 2 operating systems: types, installation, Windows configuration, and the command line.

content.intro: Know the major operating systems and how they're installed and organized.

note.text: Windows uses NTFS (permissions, journaling); exFAT/FAT32 for removable media; Linux uses ext4.

content.practice: When would you choose a clean install over an in-place upgrade?

quiz.p: Best file system for a cross-platform USB drive…
quiz.ex: exFAT works across OSes for large files.

content.intro: The Windows tools A+ techs use daily to configure and manage a system.

note.text: Keep Windows Update current; drivers via Device Manager or vendor.

content.practice: Which tool would you open to disable a startup program, and which to update a driver?

content.intro: A+ expects core commands in Windows (and awareness of Linux equivalents).

sections.code:
dir            # list files
cd folder      # change directory
ipconfig /all  # network config
ping host      # test connectivity
sfc /scannow   # repair system files
chkdsk /f      # check disk

note.text: ls, cd, ifconfig/ip, ping, cat — transferable concepts.

content.practice: Write the Windows commands to view IP config and to repair system files.

quiz.p: Which lists a directory in Windows CMD?

content.intro: A+ covers Windows plus core macOS and Linux awareness.

sections.code:
ls / cd / pwd     # navigate
sudo <cmd>        # elevate
apt install pkg   # install (Debian/Ubuntu)
chmod / chown     # permissions
ps / top          # processes

content.practice: Give the macOS backup tool and a Debian/Ubuntu package-install command.

quiz.p: Install a package on Ubuntu with…
Elevate a single Linux command with…
quiz.ex: sudo runs a command as root.

content.intro: Configuring and sharing on a Windows network.

ul: Share vs NTFS permissions (most restrictive wins)

note.text: Enable Remote Desktop only when needed; it uses port 3389.

content.practice: When combining Share and NTFS permissions, which effective permission applies?

quiz.p: A static IP is set when…
o: DHCP is unavailable or a server needs a fixed address

quiz.p: Combining Share + NTFS permissions, the effective right is…
quiz.ex: The most restrictive of the two applies.

content.intro: Local accounts, groups, and permission models.

note.text: Rename/disable default admin, enforce strong passwords + lockout, keep patched.

content.practice: Explain least privilege and how groups make it easier to apply.

courses.title: CompTIA A+: Security
courses.description: Core 2 security: threats and malware, best practices, and protecting devices and data.

content.intro: Recognize the threats A+ techs defend against and how malware spreads.

note.text: The human is the most common attack vector — train users.

p: Isolate the machine, identify/quarantine, remediate (scan/clean or reimage), educate the user.

content.practice: Match: encrypts files for payment; disguised as legitimate software; fake email to steal credentials.

quiz.p: A fake email to steal credentials is…
The most common attack vector is…

content.intro: Everyday hardening: authentication, least privilege, and safe configuration.

ul.t: — users get only what they need.

note.text: Encrypt sensitive data (BitLocker), back up (3-2-1), and wipe drives before disposal.

content.practice: Name the single highest-impact account-security control and one hardening step.

quiz.p: The biggest single account-security win is…
Before disposing of a drive you should…
quiz.ex: Wipe or destroy to prevent data recovery.

content.intro: Security isn't only digital — physical access and proper disposal matter.

note.text: 3-2-1: three copies, two media types, one offsite. Test restores.

content.practice: Give a physical control and a compliant data-destruction method.

quiz.p: Physically destroying a drive by magnetic field is…

content.intro: Securing Wi-Fi and the authentication concepts A+ expects.

note.text: Change default SSID/admin password; use a strong passphrase or enterprise auth.

content.practice: Differentiate WPA2-Personal (PSK) from WPA2-Enterprise (RADIUS).

quiz.p: The strongest listed Wi-Fi security is…

content.intro: CompTIA's structured 7-step malware removal procedure — tested in order.

ul: 6. Re-enable System Restore & create a restore point

note.text: Disable System Restore BEFORE cleaning so malware isn't preserved in restore points.

p: Quarantine stops spread; disabling restore prevents reinfection from snapshots; education prevents recurrence.
Reimage from a known-good image and restore data from clean backups.

content.practice: Why do you disable System Restore before remediation, and re-enable it after?

o: Avoid preserving malware in restore points

content.intro: The attacks that target people and networks.

note.text: User training + MFA + patching defeat most of these.

content.practice: Match: fake call, fake SMS, targeting executives — to vishing, smishing, whaling.

quiz.p: Intercepting traffic between two parties is…

courses.title: CompTIA A+: Troubleshooting
courses.description: The A+ troubleshooting methodology plus the most common hardware and software issues.

content.intro: A+ teaches a repeatable 6-step method — memorize the order.

note.text: Always back up before making changes, and change one thing at a time.

p: Ask what changed, reproduce the issue, and check the simple things first (power, cables, connectivity).
If it's beyond your scope or time, escalate with your notes — don't sit on a blocker.

content.practice: List the six troubleshooting steps in order from memory.

content.intro: Recognize the symptoms of frequent hardware failures.

p: Dust buildup, failed fans, or dried thermal paste cause throttling/shutdowns — clean and reapply paste.

note.text: No display: reseat GPU/RAM, check cable/input. Dead USB: try another port, check Device Manager.

content.practice: A PC shuts down randomly under load — list two likely hardware causes.

quiz.ex: Check seating and the video cable/input.

content.intro: The everyday software problems A+ techs resolve.

ul: Pop-ups, redirects, unknown processes, slowdowns → scan and clean/reimage

note.text: Reproduce, check recent changes, update, and apply the same 6-step method.

content.practice: A user reports a slow PC — list three things you'd check first.

quiz.p: First check for a slow PC…

quiz.ex: Use safe mode and Startup Repair.

content.intro: Diagnose connectivity like a tech using the standard tools.

sections.code:
ipconfig /all      # addressing/DNS
ping <host>        # reachability
tracert <host>     # path/hops
nslookup <name>    # DNS

note.text: Test gateway → public IP → name. If IP works but names fail, it's DNS.

content.practice: A user can ping 8.8.8.8 but no websites load — what's the likely cause and fix?

quiz.p: Ping by IP works but names fail →
Which tool shows the path/hops to a host?

content.intro: Resolve the most common printing problems.

ul.t: offline, queue stuck, connectivity — restart spooler.

p: A stuck queue blocks all jobs — restart the Print Spooler service (clears queued jobs; warn users).

note.text: Network printer offline for everyone → check the printer's power/network/IP, not one PC.

content.practice: A shared printer shows offline for everyone — where do you look first?

quiz.p: A stuck print queue is cleared by…

quiz.ex: Low toner or a dirty drum.

content.intro: Common mobile and security-symptom fixes.

ul: Pop-ups/redirects, high data use, unknown apps → scan for malware
Fake security alerts → don't click; remove the app

note.text: Reproduce, check recent installs/changes, update, then apply the 6-step method.

content.practice: A phone suddenly has high data use and pop-ups — what do you suspect and do?

quiz.p: Rapid battery drain is often caused by…
quiz.ex: Background apps or a worn battery.

quiz.p: Pop-ups + high data use on mobile suggest…
For no Wi-Fi on a phone, first try…
